# Configuration

Kaioken manages configuration across three layers: global (user-wide), per-repository, and command-line flags. This chapter explains how these layers interact to control LLM providers, models, API keys, token budgets, behavior toggles, and repository scoping.

- [Configuration Precedence](#configuration-precedence)
- [Example Configurations](#example-configurations)
- [Referenced Files](#referenced-files)

## Overview

Configuration flows from global defaults → per-repo overrides → CLI flag overrides. The system loads:
1. Global config (`$HOME/.config/kaioken/config.yaml` or `$KAIOKEN_HOME/config.yaml`) for API keys and default provider/model
2. Per-repo config (`.kaioken/config.yaml`) for model, concurrency, token limits, and file scoping
3. CLI flags for temporary overrides per invocation

All internal packages access configuration through the `config` package. The `Config` struct defines repository-specific settings, while `Global` holds user secrets and defaults.
